source_text: Apostolus dixit magis gratiam Christi quam Adae abundasse culpam; non igitur natura ab eo, non generatio, non fecunditas, sed voluntas, electio mali, morum pravitas accusatur.
pass_a_gloss: The Apostle said that the grace of Christ abounded more than Adam's fault; therefore not nature by him, not generation, not fecundity, but will, a choice of evil, a crookedness of manners is accused.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS fecunditas; Blaise blessed fertility of marriage
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: The apostle said that Christ’s grace abounded more than Adam’s fault (Romans 5:15). Thus he accuses neither nature, nor generation, nor fertility, but will, the choice of evil, and corrupt conduct.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
God-blessed fertility of the first pair; Julian will not let Paul accuse it.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
